description: Soy un junior que quiere mejorar y aprender,  estoy creando un team llamado dev brujos
summary: As the team "Dev Brujos GG," we have developed a website that helps farmers around the world—using NASA data on soil and climate conditions—to plan crop rotation, with recommendations tailored to each farmer's specific situation.
details:
What does it do?
AGRI-ORBIT is a web app that helps farmers in Latin America decide what to plant next season. Farmers describe their farm (location, soil, irrigation and priorities). The app evaluates over a thousand crop rotations using real NASA data and shows the top 5 options compared with their current rotation. It also includes a water calendar, a climate risk analysis and 1,000 Monte Carlo simulations. Its AI assistant, AGRI-AI, explains the results in plain language.

Benefits and impact
It helps farmers save water, restore soil health and reduce the risk of crop loss. It is free, bilingual (EN/ES) and works offline. Our case study is Guatemala's Dry Corridor, where drought threatens the food security of thousands of families. The model can be extended across Latin America.

Tools

  • JavaScript, HTML and CSS (MVC), Node.js and PHP, and D3.js for the 3D globe.
  • NASA data: POWER, GPM IMERG and GIBS (MODIS, SMAP, GRACE-FO, HLS).
  • AI: Google Gemini for AGRI-AI; Devin for coding; Claude and ElevenLabs for the video.

Creativity
It doesn't just show satellite data: it turns it into a concrete decision, "what to plant next". It combines our own agronomic model with an AI assistant that interprets the results without inventing data.

Factors considered
Users with limited connectivity, real and verifiable scientific data, climate change, soil and water sustainability, secure handling of AI API keys, and transparency about AI use.
